# PR #4164: Patch: the moderate levers write their bans, revocations and redemption pauses to the admin audit

Closes #4141

## What changed

Four `jackioh-server moderate` commands now each write one `admin_actions` row when they change something: `ban`, `unban`, `revoke-code` and `redemption on|off`. The row is written in the same transaction as the change. Before this, the only record was the line printed in the terminal. The dev dashboard's Audit page (`GET /api/admin/audit`) shows the new rows with no change to `apps/admin`.

- **`src/admin/store.rs`**
  - Four route constants: `CLI moderate ban`, `CLI moderate unban`, `CLI moderate revoke-code` and `CLI moderate redemption`, plus `MODERATE_ROUTES`, the list of all four.
  - `NewAdminAction.profile_id` is now `Option<String>`, and a new constructor `NewAdminAction::lever` builds a lever row.
  - `check_route` accepts exactly the four route names (an allow list, not a prefix) before its existing dev/admin rule.
  - Both stores write `None` as NULL: the Postgres store binds it as NULL, and the in-memory fake keeps it as is.
- **`src/cli/moderate.rs`**
  - One audit append beside each of the four writes, before `commit`.
  - A command that changes nothing writes no row and prints the same line as today: an `already …`, an unknown profile or code, a malformed code, or an unban of a pending account.
  - A revoked code is recorded only as `{ "codeHash": <stored hash> }`, never as the code itself.
  - The module comment that said "Stdout is the audit trail" now names both records, and the `USAGE` text says the change is also written to the audit.
- **`migrations/0095_moderation_audit.sql`** widens `admin_actions_route_check` by the same four exact names and restates the table comment. 0080 is untouched, since its checksum is pinned. The new file is listed in `MIGRATIONS`, `PINNED` (`0f1ae58d`) and `tests/sql/run.sh`.
- **`src/api/admin.rs`**: `audit()` now wraps the caller's profile id in `Some`.
- **`crates/server/README.md`**: the Moderation bullet, the audit route's row (a lever row has an empty `profileId` and `username`), and a paragraph on migration 0095.

## Tests

- **`tests/store/contract.rs`, new `mod moderate_audit`.** These run the real commands against both the in-memory store and Postgres:
  - ban, unban and the ban of a pending account each write one row with the right status before and after; the no-ops and refusals write none.
  - revoke writes the hash, and the row contains the code in none of its spellings (formatted, canonical, or with the dashes removed).
  - redemption writes a row only when the switch actually moves.
  - the route guard accepts the four routes and refuses eight near names such as `"CLI moderate ban "` or `"CLI moderate chat-reports"`.
- **`tests/store/moderate.rs`, `a_lever_whose_audit_row_fails_changes_nothing`.** With the audit write forced to fail, ban, revoke and unban each fail and change nothing, which shows the row is written in the command's own transaction.
- **`tests/api/admin.rs`, `the_moderation_levers_rows_read_back_on_the_audit_naming_no_account`.** The rows read back through `GET /api/admin/audit` with an empty `profileId` and `username`, the right before and after, and no code in plain text.
- **`tests/sql/58_moderation_audit.sql`.** In SQL, 10 near names are refused by `admin_actions_route_check`, the four lever routes are accepted with a NULL profile, and 0095 can be applied a second time without changing an existing row.

Commands run, all passing:
- `cargo test -p jackioh-server`: every binary ok (1850 passed in `server`, 754 in `server_store`).
- `sh crates/server/tests/sql/run.sh`: exit 0, and both OK lines from 58 printed.
- `sh crates/server/tests/db/run.sh`: exit 0 with 251 passed, including all four Postgres cases of `moderate_audit`.
- `cargo clippy -p jackioh-server --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo fmt --check`: clean.
- `cargo jackioh spec check`: ok.
- `cargo jackioh classify --base origin/main --claims`: `Internal` (no card plays differently, so no patch fragment).

## Decisions the issue left open

- **One route for redemption.** `CLI moderate redemption` carries `{enabled}`, and the before and after states tell on from off. I rejected a separate route for each.
- **Revoke request.** It is `{codeHash}` alone; I rejected adding the code's row id.
- **No operator name on the Audit page.** The "who" column stays empty for these rows. I rejected having the server return a label such as `operator`, because that is a change the dashboard would see, which the issue ruled out.
- **Redemption is not in the failure test.** The in-memory store keeps the redemption switch outside the tables a rollback restores. Postgres keeps it in `app.settings`, inside the transaction, so the real store is atomic; only the fake can't show it.

## Where I departed from the plan

- File 58 turns notices back on after re-applying 0095, as 57 does, so its OK line prints.
- File 58's check also confirms a dev route's row is still written.
- The longer `USAGE` footer is wrapped onto two lines.

## Worth a second look

- `check_route` now returns early on the four names. In Postgres, `actions_append` runs with an empty user id when there is no profile (`run_as(t, None)`), which the read path already does. The Postgres tests pass a real NULL into the `uuid` column.
- Re-applying 0080 by itself over lever rows would now fail its check. That never happens in practice, because the migration runner never re-runs an applied file, and `46_dev_dashboard.sql` re-applies 0080 only inside a transaction it rolls back.

# #4141: Patch: the moderate levers write their bans, revocations and redemption pauses to the admin audit
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

Today banning an account, unbanning one, revoking an invite code, or pausing invite redemption leaves its only trace in the terminal where the command ran. If that scrollback is lost, nobody can later answer "who banned this account, and when?" Every smaller dev power already writes a row the dev dashboard's Audit page shows: granting XP, filling a collection, hand-setting a rating. After this change the four big levers do too. Each ban, unban, revocation and pause or resume appears on the same Audit page with what was asked and the state before and after, for example a ban row naming the account with `active` before and `banned` after.

## Why

- These levers are the strongest in the system: they shut players out and gate entry for everyone. They deserve at least the record a dev XP grant already gets (R3074000).
- Two code facts pin the gap: `cli/moderate.rs` says "Stdout is the audit trail", while `admin_actions_append` refuses anything that is not an `/api/dev` or `/api/admin` route (`check_route` in `admin/store.rs`), and migration 0080's `admin_actions_route_check` says the same in SQL. So even a willing caller cannot record a lever run today.
- The table already fits lever rows: `profile_id` is nullable (`on delete set null`), and `Audit.tsx` renders route, request, before and after as generic text, so the dashboard shows the new rows with no admin change.

## Proposal

- Each lever run writes one `admin_actions` row in the same transaction as the change it makes: ban and unban (the account, old status into new), revoke-code (the stored code hash, never the plaintext), redemption on and off (old state into new). The actor `profile_id` is NULL: the CLI runs as the operator and holds no profile; the route names the lever (for example `CLI moderate ban`).
- A lever that changes nothing writes nothing: `already banned`, an unknown profile or code, and a refused unban of a pending account keep today's stdout line and add no row, matching how refused dev routes write nothing.
- Widen the route guard in both places it lives: `check_route` in `admin/store.rs` gains the explicit lever names (an allow-list, not a loose prefix), and a new migration widens `admin_actions_route_check` the same way, since 0080 is checksum-pinned.
- Update the `moderate.rs` header comment, which today promises stdout as the audit trail, to name both records.
- No ruling note: this is operational record-keeping, like `alerts.rs`, which carries no R-row.

## Where it lands

- `crates/server/migrations/0095_moderation_audit.sql` (0094 is the newest today): the widened route check.
- `crates/server/src/admin/store.rs`: `check_route` and a small constructor for lever rows reusing `admin_actions_append` (which already dispatches to the Postgres and fake stores together).
- `crates/server/src/cli/moderate.rs`: one append beside each of the four writes, inside its transaction.
- `crates/server/tests/store/contract.rs` and `crates/server/tests/store/moderate.rs`: fake and Postgres parity plus per-lever cases; `migrations_pinned.rs` gains the new file's line.
- No `apps/admin` change: the Audit page renders the rows as they stand. SPEC needs no change (SPEC §9.4 names the levers, §14.10 and R3074000 name the audit; neither's rule changes).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `ban`, `unban`, `revoke-code` and `redemption on|off` each write exactly one `admin_actions` row with the correct before and after when they change something, in the same transaction as the change.
- [ ] No-ops and refusals (`already banned`, unknown profile or code, pending unban) write no row and print today's stdout line unchanged.
- [ ] The rows are visible through `GET /api/admin/audit` as a dev account and on the dashboard's Audit page with no admin code change.
- [ ] No row ever carries an invite code in plaintext, only the stored hash.
- [ ] `cargo test -p jackioh-server`, `cargo clippy -p jackioh-server --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, and the `sql` suite (pinned checksums) pass.

## Size and risks

Medium: one migration, one small store addition, four call sites, and contract plus CLI tests. The main risk is the widened route check: keep it an explicit list of lever names so no other writer can smuggle rows in. The rejected alternative was a second audit table for CLI runs: it would need its own dashboard read path and trust-boundary review, while this table already has both. A decision the task left open: the operator is recorded as NULL rather than a named identity, because only holders of `DATABASE_URL` and `CODE_PEPPER` can run these commands, so who reduces to who holds the production environment, as today.
